summary: Request: time-boxed breakglass access for staging KMS failure-mode test (disable/deny scenarios)
description:
Requesting temporary breakglass access in the staging AWS environment to execute the KMS failure-mode test harness.

Requester: Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Operators needing access (time-boxed): Sean Gallagher (SRE), Emily Zhao (Data-plane Eng)
Scope: Staging only. No production access requested.

Business justification:
- Required to simulate KMS dependency failures (AccessDenied, DisabledKey, throttling) during the scheduled game-day for the KMS hardening project.
- Testing requires controlled actions that are not possible with standard least-privilege roles (e.g., temporarily disabling a staging CMK, applying a deny statement, and restoring).

Requested access:
- AWS IAM role: arn:aws:iam::4729XXXXXXX:role/BreakglassKMSAdmin (staging account)
- Permissions required: kms:DisableKey, kms:EnableKey, kms:PutKeyPolicy, kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion (NOT requested), kms:CancelKeyDeletion (NOT requested), kms:DescribeKey, kms:ListResourceTags, kms:GetKeyPolicy
- Explicit exclusions: no ability to create new CMKs for prod; no cross-account assume; no access to customer data stores.

Time window:
- Start: 2026-01-19 10:00 PT
- End: 2026-01-19 14:00 PT

Audit / evidence requirements (per breakglass policy):
- Approval recorded in this ticket by Security (Marcus Lin) and acknowledged by GRC (Olga Petrov or delegate).
- All actions must be executed via role assumption (no long-lived keys). MFA required.
- CloudTrail evidence to be captured and referenced here (event IDs + timestamps) for: DisableKey/EnableKey and any PutKeyPolicy changes.
- Post-test: confirm role access removed, key restored to baseline policy, and a short summary of actions/outcomes added to this ticket.

Notes:
- Test plan reference: ENG-4234 (failure-mode matrix) and the KMS dependency degradation runbook.
